Instrument (EN): Perceived Parental Autonomy Support and Control Scale — Russian adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Perceived Parental Autonomy Support: Choice Within Limits (4); Meaningful Rationale (4); Acknowledgment of Feelings (4). Controlling Parenting: Threats to Punish (4); Guilt-Inducing Criticism (4); Performance Pressure (4). Two higher-order constructs, not diagnostic scores.
Research provenance: Gordeeva T.O., Nechaeva D.M., Sychev O.A.; Psychology. Journal of the Higher School of Economics 23(1):42-61 (2026), DOI 10.17323/1813-8918-2026-1-42-61. Russian adaptation of Mageau et al. 2015 P-PASS; N979 main study (728 university +251 secondary students), independent retest N92. Six first-order scales and 2 higher-order factors; original developer website explicitly marks P-PASS for personal use only.
DB locales: No P-PASS parent or edition published in live app.assessment_versions: verified by read-only definition_key search 2026-10-24.
EN form: Original French/English P-PASS exists; current study does not validate a new English edition. Original author states personal use only.
RU form: RU-RU validated respondent translation studied among young people N979 with retest N92; first published Russian adaptation in 2026.
ES form: No ES respondent form validated in this study.
Other translations: Other versions including French, Italian and Romanian are listed by original author's laboratory; their rights and validation require individual verification.
Target population: Russian-speaking high-school students and university young adults, mean ages 16.38 (n251) and 20.03 (n728); measure perception of parents, NOT parental direct self-report.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: PERSONAL USE ONLY on original developer lab website https://mapageweb.umontreal.ca/mageaug/echelles.htm ; commercial digital/SaaS rights NOT granted. Written permission required from original P-PASS rightsholders and Russian adaptors for items, online administration and scoring.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Do not publish proprietary 24 item wording or scores; minors require parental consent/safety and age-specific interpretation; original developer personal-use restriction explicitly recorded.

Instrument (EN): School Connectedness Scale — Portuguese adolescents revised four-item edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): School Connectedness / school belonging (single factor); revised version no longer directly captures teacher fairness or a separate teacher-connectedness subscale.
Research provenance: Maçãs-Carvalho I., Rijo D., Brazão N., Canavarro M.C. et al., School Mental Health 18:688-700, published 2026-03-16, DOI 10.1007/s12310-026-09863-5. N621 public-school adolescents in Portugal ages 11-18. Original 5-item unidimensional model had poor fit; revised 4-item CFA improved fit, internal consistency satisfactory; sex-based measurement invariance supported.
DB locales: Neither SCS-school 4-item nor this revised PT-PT edition published in live app.assessment_versions; verified by definition_key search 2026-10-24.
EN form: English parent 5-item School Connectedness Scale discussed in article; no new English edition evaluated.
RU form: No Russian respondent version validated in this article.
ES form: No Spanish respondent version validated here; distinct from MDS3 Spanish 14-item school connectedness research edition.
Other translations: PT-PT Portuguese adolescent survey study provides edition-specific empirical evidence for revised 4-item solution; article does not establish a new 2026 translation or PT-BR equivalence.
Target population: 621 Portuguese public-school adolescents aged 11 to 18 years; not general adult or clinical populations.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Open-access CC BY article is not automatic commercial SaaS license for parent instrument or translated items. Seek original instrument owner and Portuguese research team written permission for hosting, wording and scoring; children's privacy and consent required.
Validated edition evidence / links: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12310-026-09863-5 ; original 5-item vs final 4-item evidence in Results/CFA.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Critically distinguish this 4-item single-factor instrument from MDS3 14-item three-factor school-connectedness subscale. Do not reuse parent 5-item scoring unchanged or claim teacher-relationship coverage.
